B. Is this measure already running in Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county (or in the Tyks university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Stereotactic radiotherapy pathway for early cancer in patients who cannot be operated. Every stage I patient who is too frail for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy (3-8 visits, no anaesthesia) instead of being left without treatment. The treatment exists in every university hospital; what is missing in some counties is the referral rule.
effect_summary_en: In the Netherlands, 7% fewer elderly stage I patients went untreated once stereotactic radiotherapy became available; the study does not report the gain as a share of all lung cancer patients.
supported_en: A Netherlands Cancer Registry study (Annals of Oncology 2012, 4605 patients) found 7% fewer elderly stage I patients went untreated once stereotactic radiotherapy was fully available.
not_supported_en: The study does not show the 0.8-point gain across all lung cancer patients, and it does not show a Finnish effect.

missing_en: No page shows a rule that every inoperable stage I patient from Ostrobothnia is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy.
summary_en: Varha/Tyks (news item, 21 Nov 2024) says stereotactic radiotherapy can be used as first-line treatment instead of surgery in lung cancer. It also says Tyks treats about 160 patients a year with stereotactic techniques, across all cancers and not only lung cancer. No Tyks or Ostrobothnia page shows a rule that every frail stage I patient is referred for it. A Dutch registry study (2012) found 7% fewer elderly stage I patients went untreated once stereotactic radiotherapy was available, which is only indirect support for the 0.8-point assumption.
unanswered_en: I found no page with a referral rule, and none saying whether Vaasa central hospital gives stereotactic lung radiotherapy itself; the Vaasa hospital page did not load.
